    Graded decomposition (Lemma 6.3(1)) #

    "Every finite graded A₀-module is a sum of shifts of the M_i. […] Decompose its underlying ungraded module into normalized modules M_i. Write the projections and inclusions as p_a and j_a, so 1_X = Σ_a p_a j_a. Taking homogeneous degree-zero parts gives 1_X = Σ_{a,r} (p_a)_r (j_a)_{-r}."

    Deviation in the proof: instead of the locality of End_gr(X) for a graded indecomposable X, we split off one shifted M_W at a time from a graded idempotent e (exists_summand). Some composite (p_a)_r (j_b)_{-r} of equal level is nonzero, hence invertible by eq:normalized-hom-degrees (exists_inv); otherwise the level sums E_r satisfy E_r E_s = 0 for r ≤ s and force e = 0. The result (exists_gdecomp) is a finite family of graded inclusions and projections with Σ inc_a pr_a = 1, which is the input of extVanish_of_decomp.

    References #

    • Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras, https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations. Numbered statements cited here refer to it.
